notes: first visit this season- landed with helicopter- low HS values to road. Layer Notes (header): '87-69cm: sintering, aggregrations' (sic); '87-69cm: Problematic layer'; '43.5-28cm: sintering, aggregates'; '28-20cm: sintering, aggregates'. Stability tests column: 'CT9, SC @87cm JAN 30 FC 1.5'. Chart title 'Simpson Study Full'.
summary: 117 cm HS: DH 0-28 cm (2-8 mm; 1F+ then P-) under FC 28-43.5 cm (1F, 1.5-10 mm), a 0.5 cm hard IF crust at 43.5-44 cm (P), FC 44-69 cm (1F+/1F), a 18 cm FCxr 69-87 cm flagged problematic layer (F+) with CT9 SC at its top (87 cm, "JAN 30 FC 1.5"), FCxr 87-96, RGsr 96-109, DF 109-116 and a 1 cm moist K crust at the surface; warm spring snowpack (air +2.5, -0.8 at 10 cm to -5.2 at 107 cm); PF 60, PS 25
reading_issues: Date: the header prints 01/03/2025 (DD/MM/YYYY) so the pit is 1 March 2025, not 3 Jan (air temperature +2.5 degC, HS 117 cm and the "JAN 30 FC" test comment also fit March). Hardness bar edges, layer boundaries and temperature dots measured from native pixels against the axis ticks; measured boundaries sit about 0.15 cm above whole numbers, so they are rounded to 20, 28, 43.5, 44, 55, 69, 87, 96, 109, 116 and 117 cm (43.5 is confirmed by the layer note "43.5-28cm"). Table rows for the thin top layer and the 43.5-44 cm crust are stretched with connector lines. Glyphs: single-dash (IF) for the 116-117 cm crust and the surface row, double-bar "=" read as an ice formation (rain-crust style) for the 43.5-44 cm layer, tiny dot read as RGsr for 96-109 cm, rounded-top squares with centre line read as FCxr for 69-96 cm; sub-types of IF/RG are not certain. No temperature points at the ground or the surface (first dot at 107 cm, i.e. 10 cm depth). The 28-43.5 cm layer has no moisture entry. The CT9 SC at 87 cm sits at the top of the 69-87 cm problematic layer; layer_grain recorded as FC.
